 VGK Lead NHL In Percentage Of Points From Forwards, Raising Questions About Expensive Blue Line 
 By Ken Boehlke 
 On November 7, 2026 
 In Stats 
 (Photo Credit: SinBin.vegas Photographer Brandon Andreasen)
 On Thursday night, former Golden Knight defenseman and 2nd round draft pick Kaedan Korczak earned his 10th assist of the regular season. The number is jarring because not only would he lead all Vegas defensemen with that number, but he has double the point total of offensive dynamo Shea Theodore.
 It’s really not about Korczak, though, as during his time in Vegas he wasn’t exactly an offensive weapon, scoring just 37 points in 155 games. Nonetheless, there is something to say about Vegas lack of offense from the highly paid blue line.
 VGK have received just six goals and 28 points from defensemen in the 18 games played so far this season. It’s a stunningly low total, which currently ranks 29th overall and 30th on a per game basis.
 This season, forwards have accounted for 82.4% of the Golden Knights’ points, the highest share in the NHL by three percentage points and easily on pace to be the highest in franchise history.
 Season Forward Goal% Forward Assist% Forward Points% 
 2026-27 89.8% 78.0% 82.4% 
 2025–26 86.0% 75.6% 79.4% 
 2024–25 87.2% 67.7% 74.9% 
 2023–24 89.7% 66.5% 74.9% 
 2022–23 86.5% 68.9% 75.5% 
 2021–22 80.5% 69.0% 73.4% 
 2020–21 81.1% 67.0% 72.2% 
 2019–20 84.8% 72.0% 77.0% 
 2018–19 84.6% 68.1% 74.4% 
 2017–18 86.2% 67.5% 74.5% 
 There are two ways to look at these numbers. First, the more optimistic view.
 The season VGK won the Cup, they received 75.5% of their points from forwards, but that number increased to 79.8% in the playoffs. VGK defensemen scored just 9.1% of the goals on that run as well, similar to this year’s 10.2%. So, clearly the Golden Knights don’t require goals and points from defensemen to win the biggest games of the year.
 On the flip side, though, the Golden Knights are investing a lot of money into offensive-minded defensemen. Shea Theodore, Noah Hanifin, and Rasmus Andersson combine to make up 22.3% of the salary cap. Their combined 17 points make up just 10.7% of Vegas’ total offense. All the while, the Golden Knights currently rank #2 in the league with 123 long-range shot attempts, a whopping 35 more than the league average.
 Also, VGK’s defensive numbers have dropped significantly since the blue line scoring slowed down. Over the first 10 games, VGK defensemen scored all six of their goals and 20 of the 28 points. In those games, the Golden Knights were allowing just 2.40 goals per game. In the last eight games, when the blue line has not scored a goal and registered just eight assists, they’ve allowed 3.13 goals per game.
 It’s probably not necessary for VGK to be one of the teams receiving the most offense from their blue line, however, the defensemen are clearly involved in the attack and firing tons of pucks from the blue line towards the goal. Those shots are not turning into goals to this point, however.
 The more involved Vegas’ blue line is on the game, the better they are both offensively and defensively. It’s probably the easiest way out of the current scoring lull, though, sometimes it’s easier said than done.
